name: Runemaster Hurricane lands on the terrain on inclines (#7825)
contract: #7825: Runemaster Hurricane (645435) teleports the Runemaster around the target once per strike (1.5 yd ring, 5 directions) and used the target's Z for every landing, so a strike landing uphill on an incline put the player inside the terrain and under the map, which can kill a Hardcore character.

StrikeHurricane in AscensionRunemasterHurricane.cpp now clamps each landing to the map height at the destination (Map::GetHeight with MAX_HEIGHT, falling back to the target's Z when no height exists), the same ground-clamp the .go teleport path uses. The clamp sits in the single shared strike function, so both Hurricane (645435) and Runic Hurricane (280930) land on the surface.

This scenario runs the real cast path at the reporter's incline (map 0, -9190.03 -2319.81): after the ability ends on its own it snapshots the map height under the player (ground_height) and asserts position_z equals it (ratio 1.0 within float tolerance). Pre-fix landings keep the target's Z, which on this incline sits below the terrain surface; post-fix landings are set from the height query itself, so the ratio is exact.

Socketless sessions have no client fall physics: a bad landing keeps its teleported Z server-side instead of falling, which is exactly what the position_z/ground_height comparison observes. Strike destinations are Z-independent in X/Y (angles from facing, 1.5 yd ring), so the final landing X/Y is identical pre/post fix and only Z differs; the dummy-Z snapshot below lets the report state the pre-fix ratio arithmetically. map_id pins the comparison to map 0, and a strike-damage assert keeps the ability itself working.
Executed post-fix: 5 strikes land, final ground 89.824, position_z ratio exactly 1.0 — PASSED.
